title: Nevermore

location.name: Ruins Shore and the Night Garden Fields (Center zone)
location.kind: night beach strewn with chapel wreckage and ash, a trail up a dune incline to moonlit garden fields
location.real_analog: a Delmarva barrier-beach shore (e.g. Assateague, Maryland) with burned pine behind the dunes and farm fields of sunflowers or mustard just inland

situation: The POET, now in a red/black outfit with sunglasses and no heart, hands always in his pockets, walks the night shore past the chapel's shattered remnants and wildfire ash while ravens fly overhead. He finds his heart on the sand; without using his hands it floats up and re-enters him. He follows a trail up to a moonlit field, walks through it, searches the shadows for his hands, finds them, puts them back on, and stands in the field reflecting until 'Now go.'
time_of_day: night / twilight, deepening to full dark in the field
weather_light: twilight-to-night on the shore, calm waves and still wind; moonlight on the field, then clouds hide the stars for the deepest darkness; golden glow from the plants

lines: What if i followed this / trail
broken pieces have / washed ashore—
the ashes of / expired wildfires
lifted from the night sea / water's floor.

level of silence

set_pieces.name: Night garden field

the plants in a golden / hue bloom & faced toward / me
the weeds repel,

set_pieces.what_happens: Clouds hide the stars; POET searches the bare ground in the shadows for his two hands, finds them and puts them back on.
lines: The clouds mute the stars
to search the bare ground / for two hands—
& they too / used to be mine.
I put them / back on

set_pieces.name: Standing in the field
set_pieces.what_happens: POET stands in the field reflecting, heart and hands restored, then is told to go.
lines: nevermore.
I have won at the world / & lost my soul—
I want nothing more / that to just be / myself—
Now go.
set_pieces.camera: static frontal medium-wide, still tree and field behind; slow push in
set_pieces.position: center of the field near a still tree

arrival.from_previous: Treatment: 'Cut to POET' on the same shore where the chapel remnants and shattered tambourine lie.

departure.to_next: 'Now go.' - still night, he walks on through the field into the welcoming parade of afro-futuristic ancestors (Bloodlines).

encoding: The beach is where the broken engagement washed up, so the POET can only begin recovering among its debris: the heart he finds there is the first thing he takes back. The climb from sea level to the field turns grief into ascent, and the field's soil is where lost hands (his capacity to act and touch) are buried. Inferred: shore = what was lost, field = what is grown back, and leaving the field on foot sets up the ancestors who meet him in Bloodlines.
